summary: Natural, light Dutch; one confirmed restricted construction (conjunction 'nu' in b080) forces a round. The vocabulary FAIL is tool-driven: 'haarnetje' and 'drugsgeld' are transparent compounds of known parts, so the real new-lemma density is 2 stretch words (~8/1000), inside budget. Secondary: the shouted line deviates from the glossary, one colon sentence carries four finite verbs, and the two similes in b085 read as compressed translations.

findings.problem: 'nu' used as a subordinating conjunction (now that) is outside the allowed subordinator list.
findings.evidence: flag R-CONJ-OTHER (likely 0.85) confirmed; allowed.md A-SUB lists als/omdat/zodra/zodat/terwijl/hoewel/nadat/toen/voordat only.
findings.required_fix: Use the allowed subordinator: 'Dat was…eigenlijk best \gl{gênant}{embarrassing}, als hij het zo bekeek.' (R-CONJ-OTHER move 4; same idiom as 'als je het zo bekijkt').

findings.problem: Fixed glossary line not used; the edition renders this shout one way everywhere.
findings.evidence: glossary.json 'owl': 'Can I get an owl?' = 'Mag ik een uil?'; bible.md ch 1 traps repeat it.
findings.required_fix: Replace with “\emph{Brief voor Zweinstein! Mag ik een uil?}”.

findings.fragment: Pas toen bedacht hij iets: als er echt een uil naar beneden kwam en de brief greep, dan moest hij dat aan pap vertellen.
findings.problem: One sentence of 24 words with four finite verbs (bedacht, kwam, greep, moest); the colon hides it from the load check.
findings.evidence: L-VERBS: at most three finite verbs per sentence; L-LEN soft limit 20.
findings.required_fix: Full stop instead of the colon: 'Pas toen bedacht hij iets. Als er \emph{echt} een uil naar beneden kwam en de brief greep, dan moest hij dat aan pap vertellen.'

findings.fragment: trok zijn hand omlaag als uit het vuur
findings.problem: 'als uit het vuur' is not a Dutch idiom; the compressed simile reads as a translation and makes the reader re-parse (as if the hand came out of a fire).
findings.evidence: No Dutch collocation 'als uit het vuur'; the natural form needs 'alsof' (R-CONJ-OTHER), so the comparison must be made explicit instead.
findings.required_fix: Make the comparison explicit with an allowed frame: 'Harry trok zijn hand omlaag, zo snel als uit een vuur, en verstopte de envelop achter zijn rug als drugsgeld.' Optionally detach the second simile as a fragment for rhythm: '… achter zijn rug. Als drugsgeld.'

findings.problem: Two glosses in a 12-word paragraph on words the lexicon already marks as known.
findings.evidence: lexicon: schor = known A2 (c3529), gefluister = known A2 (c4473); gloss_per_paragraph_max 2 reached on known words.
findings.required_fix: Drop the gloss on 'schor' (write 'een schor \gl{gefluister}{whisper}'); the gloss on gefluister may stay only because exceptions.json asks to gloss fluisteren at first occurrence.

findings.problem: Tool rates it hard (nt2lex C1); for the reader it is a transparent compound of two A1 words and the bible fixes the rendering.
findings.evidence: lexicon: drug = known A1, geld = known A1; bible.md ch 1 traps: 'drug money' → drugsgeld; 'replace-or-gloss' action dismissed.
findings.required_fix: No change; leave unglossed. Lexicon owner: add 'drugsgeld' as known compound or let compound decomposition override an nt2lex-only hard status.

findings.problem: Tool lemma 'haarne' is a mis-lemmatised diminutive; the word is haar + net + -je, all known.
findings.evidence: lexicon: haar known, net (NOUN) known A1; vocabulary row 'haarne' status unknown dismissed.
findings.required_fix: No change. Lexicon owner: add 'haarnetje' (or teach the tool -tje stripping).

findings.problem: Unknown lemma, but it carries the scene (embarrassment comedy) and has no plain equivalent with the same meaning for this reader.
findings.evidence: lexicon: gênant absent; 'pijnlijk' (B1) was learned as 'painful', 'stom' shifts the meaning; already glossed.
findings.required_fix: Keep as is. Lexicon owner: consider adding gênant (very frequent spoken word).

findings.problem: Unknown lemma; the plain alternative 'hek' (A2) is an open fence, and the image needs a solid one she must peer over.
findings.evidence: lexicon: schutting absent, hek known A2 'fence'; already glossed; block at the 2-gloss limit.
findings.required_fix: Keep as is; switch to 'het hek van de buren' only if the gloss budget of b086 is needed elsewhere.

findings.fragment: Mevrouw~Figg, af en toe de oppas.
findings.problem: 'af en toe de oppas' is a slightly stiff ellipsis; the possessive reads more naturally.
findings.evidence: Native pattern: 'af en toe zijn oppas' / 'soms zijn oppas'.
findings.required_fix: Prefer 'Mevrouw~Figg, af en toe zijn oppas.'

findings.problem: Gloss on a word the lexicon marks known (pluk = handful, tuft, A2); the slot could be freed.
findings.required_fix: Optional: remove the gloss if b086 ever needs a second gloss elsewhere; otherwise leave.

findings.fragment: ook als ik me dan dom voel
findings.problem: The particle 'dan' inside the als-clause is a small spoken-Dutch filler; without it the clause is cleaner.
findings.evidence: 'ook als ik me dom voel' is the plain form; 'dan' adds nothing a reader needs.
findings.required_fix: Optional: 'ook als ik me dom voel'.

findings.problem: Two B1 stretch lemmas in the scene, inside the budget.
findings.evidence: stretch budget 2 vs 8/1000 allowed; both transparent (achter+deur; hersenen recurs for 'brain' per translator note).

flag_decisions.reason: 'nu' as a subordinator (now that) is not in the allowed list A-SUB; the translator's own notes in V2/V3 replace it with 'als'. likely → must_fix (L1).
Attributive 'verbaasd' is a plain adjective: lexicon ADJ A1 and named explicitly in restricted.md ('verbaasd … are fine'); look-alike table 'Hij was verbaasd.'

tool_feedback: R-PARTICIPLE on 'verbaasde' (b084) is a false positive: lemma is a lexicon ADJ entry and restricted.md names 'verbaasd' as allowed; skip amod participles whose lemma is a lexicon ADJ, or push confidence under ignore_confidence (0.3).
Vocabulary row 'haarne' is a non-word: spaCy lemma of the diminutive 'haarnetje'; strip -tje/-je before lookup and retry compound decomposition (haar + net) on the stripped form.

'drugsgeld' rated hard C1 (pos VERB) from an nt2lex-only hit; the lexicon hit pre-empts compound decomposition, so a transparent compound of two A1 words is reported as hard. Try decomposition before accepting an nt2lex-only hard status with no cards, or when the POS is implausible.

Load check missed the 4-finite-verb sentence in b076 because the colon is treated as a sentence boundary (27 vs 26 sentences in V2); either count the colon-joined sentence or document the colon as an accepted split.

Glosses on known lemmas (schor, gefluister, plukken, wilskracht-compound) are invisible: they appear only in per_block.glosses, never as a row, so gloss bloat on known words cannot be seen from the table. Add a 'glossed known lemma' row or warning.
Density verdict HIGH (16.7/1000) counts 'haarne' and 'drugsgeld' as new; after the two fixes above the scene is 2 stretch lemmas ≈ 8.4/1000 and passes.
